title: Notes to Financial Statements - Disclosure Requirements

content.purpose_of_notes: Provide information essential to understanding financial statements. Notes are integral part of financial statements.
content.fundamental_principle: If information is essential for fair presentation, it must be disclosed in notes (not optional)
typical_notes_included: Summary of significant accounting policies (Note 1 typically)
Detailed information about balance sheet accounts
Detailed information about income statement items

note_1_accounting_policies.purpose: Describe accounting principles and methods used
required_disclosures: Inventory valuation method (FIFO, weighted average, etc.)
note_1_accounting_policies.principle: Disclose any policies that involve judgment or choice between alternatives

common_required_disclosures.property_plant_equipment: Major classes, depreciation methods, useful lives
common_required_disclosures.inventories: Valuation method, major categories (raw materials, WIP, finished goods)
common_required_disclosures.equity: Classes of stock (authorized, issued, outstanding), par values, preferences
common_required_disclosures.income_taxes: Components of tax expense, deferred tax assets/liabilities, effective rate reconciliation
common_required_disclosures.pension_plans: Components of pension expense, funded status, assumptions
common_required_disclosures.leases: Future lease payments, lease terms, significant assumptions
common_required_disclosures.commitments_contingencies: Nature and amount of commitments, contingent liabilities

subsequent_events.type_i_recognized: Events providing additional evidence about conditions existing at balance sheet date → Adjust financial statements
subsequent_events.type_ii_disclosed: Events arising after balance sheet date → Disclose in notes (do not adjust)
subsequent_events.evaluation_period: Through financial statement issuance date (public companies) or availability date (private companies)
examples_type_i: Settlement of litigation (outcome provides evidence of condition at BS date)
Bankruptcy of customer (receivable collectibility at BS date)
examples_type_ii: Sale of major asset after year-end
Loss from fire or natural disaster after year-end

related_party_disclosures.required: Nature of relationship, description of transactions, dollar amounts
related_party_disclosures.definition: Affiliates, principal owners, management, immediate families
related_party_disclosures.cannot_state: Cannot state transactions were on arm's-length terms unless can be substantiated

segment_reporting.disclose: Revenues, profit/loss, assets for reportable segments. Reconciliation to consolidated.

fair_value_disclosures.required_for_all: Fair value hierarchy level (1, 2, 3) for all fair value measurements
fair_value_disclosures.level_3: Enhanced disclosures (valuation techniques, inputs, sensitivities, transfers)

accounting_changes_and_errors.retrospective_changes: Nature, reason, effect on prior periods
accounting_changes_and_errors.error_corrections: Nature of error, effect on prior periods

earnings_per_share.if_complex_capital_structure: Disclose reconciliation of numerator and denominator for basic and diluted EPS
earnings_per_share.antidilutive_securities: Describe securities excluded from diluted EPS as antidilutive

loss_contingencies.reasonably_possible: Disclose nature and amount (or range, or statement that cannot estimate)

concentration_of_credit_risk.financial_instruments: Disclose significant concentrations of credit risk (group of counterparties in same industry/region)

comparative_statements.presentation: If presenting comparative statements (prior year), notes should cover both periods

materiality.qualitative_factors: Not just quantitative threshold. Consider nature of item and context.

cpa_exam_tips: Note 1: Summary of significant accounting policies (required for all entities)
Use of estimates: Required disclosure in Note 1
Subsequent events: Type I = adjust FS. Type II = disclose only.
Related parties: Disclose nature, transactions, amounts. Cannot claim arm's-length unless substantiated.
Loss contingencies: Probable = accrue + disclose. Reasonably possible = disclose only.
Fair value: Disclose hierarchy level (1, 2, 3) for all FV measurements
Notes are integral part of financial statements (not optional)

key_points: Notes are integral part of financial statements, essential for fair presentation
Note 1: Significant accounting policies (basis of consolidation, depreciation, inventory, revenue recognition, etc.)
Required disclosures: PPE, inventory, debt, equity, income taxes, pensions, leases, contingencies
Subsequent events: Type I (adjust FS), Type II (disclose only)
Related parties: Disclose nature, transactions, amounts
Fair value: Disclose hierarchy levels for all FV measurements
Loss contingencies: Probable = accrue + disclose. Reasonably possible = disclose.
